# Maghadevajātaka (Ja 9)
**ID:** Ja 9
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Maghadevajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja9
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maghadevajātaka* (Ja 9) is a narrative in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Appleton 2010; Berkwitz 2013]. Set at Jetavana, the Buddha relates the story to illustrate the Great Renunciation [SuttaCentral]. In this past birth, the Bodhisatta was King Makhādeva (or Maghadeva), who voluntarily abandons his throne, luxurious life, and royal possessions upon finding his first grey hair, retreating to a mango grove to embrace the solitary life of an ascetic and cultivate meditative practice [Narada 2008; Wood 2005; Appleton 2010; Dhammadinna 2013].
The text holds an established place in early Buddhist narrative literature, visual art, and later vernacular adaptations. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang recorded a stūpa in Madhya Deśa associated with the Cakravartin Mahādeva's renunciation upon seeing a grey hair [Wood 2005]. The jātaka also appears in early Indian sculptural coping narratives, where the Bodhisattva king is depicted seated on an armchair signifying royal status before becoming an ascetic [Wood 2005]. In Sri Lanka, the classical Sinhala poetic work *Muvadevdāvata* was composed directly based on this jātaka [Berkwitz 2013].
Within the Pali canon, this narrative corresponds closely to the *Maghadeva Sutta* of the Majjhima Nikāya (MN 83) as well as the later *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541), though the canonical sutta version does not contain the jātaka verses [SuttaCentral; Appleton 2010; Dhammadinna 2013]. SuttaCentral identifies further parallels in the Chinese Āgamas (*Madhyama-āgama* MĀ 67, *Ekottarika-āgama* EĀ 50.4, as well as T 152.87 and T 211.38), the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (Up 2.050 / d1), and resembling texts (EĀ 1.1 and T 744) [SuttaCentral; Dhammadinna 2013]. DharmaNexus records no substantial text-reuse matches for this entry [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels (SuttaCentral): MN 83 (PTS MN ii 74) Maghadeva Sutta; EA 50.4; Ja 541 Nimijātaka; MA 67 大天㮈林; T 152.87 摩調王; T 211.38 法句譬喻經道利品第三十八; Up 2.050
- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): d1 འདུལ་བ་གཞི།  (Vinaya-vastu)
- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): EA 1.1 序; T 744 除恐災患
